sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 covers southeastern Lodi and the adjoining northwest corner of Hasbrouck Heights at 100 feet to an inch, with the grid turned about 52 degrees on the page so that Prospect Street and Woodside Avenue run across it. In the upper half, in Lodi, Prospect Street, Mercer Place, Orchard Street and Grove Street are crossed by Hunter Street, Autumn Street, Spring Street, James Street, South Place, Washington Street, Liberty Street and Union Street, with Roosevelt Avenue, Hillcrest Avenue, Madison Place and Jackson Place entering from the left. The blocks are residential, mostly frame dwellings with private garages and coops. Institutions include the Reformed Dutch Church on Washington Street, the Christian Reformed Church and parsonage on Liberty Street, St. Francis de Sales Roman Catholic church, rectory and club house on Union Street, the Lodi fire department (Hose Co. No. 1, Rescue Hook and Ladder Co. No. 1) on Prospect Street, the Dansen Construction Co. yard on South Place and a bowling alley. The Lodi and Hasbrouck Heights borough line crosses the lower half along Grove Street, Tripola Street, a lot line west of La Salle Avenue and a line between Ottawa and Paterson Avenues, and follows Woodside Avenue. South of it, in Hasbrouck Heights, Tripola, Jefferson, Brookside and Woodside Avenues cross La Salle, Ottawa, Paterson, Bell and Lawrence Avenues and Madison Avenue: long blocks laid out in lots with only scattered dwellings. Spring Street becomes Ottawa Avenue and James Street curves into Paterson Avenue south of Grove Street. Shanley Place, James Place and Leo Place run off Union Street at the right edge. The scale bar is printed in Woodside Avenue.
notes: Tripola (Ottawa Avenue to Hunter Street) is modern Austin Place.
Ottawa Avenue north of Grove Street is modern Spring Street; Paterson Avenue continues north as James Street; Lawrence Avenue continues north as Liberty Street.
Shanley Place has no match in the OpenStreetMap extract.
The scale bar is printed in Woodside Avenue; the La Salle Avenue / Woodside Avenue junction was excluded because the detector paired a street edge with it.

Lodi and Hasbrouck Heights at the borough line, 100 ft. One part (sheet-16). Prospect, Mercer Pl, Orchard, Grove, Tripola (Austin Pl), Jefferson, Brookside, Woodside Avs; Hunter, Autumn, Spring/Ottawa, James/Paterson, South Pl, Washington, Liberty/Lawrence, Union; La Salle, Bell. Scale bar printed in Woodside Av.

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 covers the northwest corner of Lodi, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 66 degrees on the page. Harrison Avenue runs along the top edge, with the Garfield borough line drawn down its middle; a second stretch of the Garfield line follows Frederick Street on the left. Inside, parallel streets (Farnham Avenue, Westminster Place, Westervelt Place, Burns Avenue, Corabelle Place and Corabelle Avenue, Dell-Glen Avenue and Berenice Place) cross Frederick Street, Charles Street, Bryant Place, Home Place, Walnut Place, Park Avenue, 1st Street and Myrtle Street. Passaic Avenue crosses the lower half diagonally from Terrace Avenue towards a steel bridge over the Saddle River in the bottom right corner, and Garfield Place runs parallel to it further west. The area is residential: blocks of narrow lots with frame dwellings, scattered brick or stores along Harrison Avenue, Charles Street and Passaic Avenue, a Mt. Virgin Sisters' house and a hall on Harrison Avenue, a bakery, a fire department house with a hand hose reel on Charles Street, a lumber yard and a beer garden. Roosevelt School stands on Park Avenue at Passaic Avenue. Lodi Cemetery and the Bnai Jacob Cemetery fill the large block between Terrace Avenue and Home Place. River Place, along the Saddle River, is marked not opened. Water pipes and their sizes are drawn in most streets.
notes: Dell-Glen Avenue is modern River Street; Berenice Place is modern Bernice Place.
Corabelle Place (Park Avenue to 1st Street) is modern South Corabelle Avenue; Garfield Place is modern Garfield Avenue.
The Garfield borough line runs down the middle of Harrison Avenue; the detector paired it with a street edge, so the four Harrison Avenue junctions were excluded.
Roosevelt School, Lodi Cemetery and Bnai Jacob Cemetery are named on the sheet.

Lodi, northwest at the Garfield line, 100 ft. One part (sheet-17). Harrison Av (Garfield line drawn down its middle; its junctions excluded), Farnham, Westminster, Westervelt, Burns, Corabelle, Dell Glen (modern River St), Berenice (Bernice Pl); Frederick, Charles, Bryant, Home, Walnut, Park, 1st, Myrtle; Passaic and Garfield Pl (Garfield Av) diagonals; Terrace Av; Lodi Cemetery. Pilot sheet.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 covers north central Lodi east of sheet 17, at 100 feet to an inch, with the street grid turned about 66 degrees on the page. Harrison Avenue crosses the top with the Garfield borough line along it; beyond it a strip of Garfield (block 124, Grennelle Avenue) is drawn. Below, Farnham Avenue, Westminster Place, Westervelt Place, Burns Avenue, Corabelle Avenue and Dell-Glen Place run across the sheet, crossed by Leonard (lettered Loenard) and Willard Streets on the left, Arnot Street in the middle and Hughes and Warren Streets on the right. The upper half is residential, mostly frame dwellings on narrow lots, with the borough water works and pumping station, a 500,000 gallon reservoir and a steel water tower on Arnot Street at Farnham Avenue, and a hall on Arnot Street. The lower half is dominated by the United Piece Dye Works (dyeing, printing and dye manufacturing), drawn in detail: two reservoirs and a well reservoir on Corabelle Avenue, the mill race, a coal pile, chemical pits, and long sprinklered brick dye, printing, finishing and examining buildings on both sides of the Saddle River, with a hospital, laboratory, auto repair garage and an I.D.P.L. hall on Dell-Glen Place. Arnot Street turns diagonally to cross the river by a bridge. A railroad crosses the bottom of the sheet near Mercer Street, New Street, Cottage Place and Nicholson Street, which belong to sheets 19 and 20.
notes: Leonard Street is lettered Loenard on the sheet.
Dell-Glen Place is modern Dell Glen Avenue.
United Piece Dye Works (Mutual Risk) fills the lower half of the sheet.
Borough water works, pumping station and reservoir on Arnot Street at Farnham Avenue.

Lodi, north centre, 100 ft. One part (sheet-18). Harrison, Farnham, Westminster, Westervelt, Burns, Corabelle, Dell-Glen Pl (Dell Glen Av); Leonard (lettered Loenard), Willard, Arnot, Hughes, Warren; United Piece Dye Works and the Saddle River across the lower half.

sheet-19-1.description: The main part of sheet 19 shows the centre of Lodi around Main Street at the larger scale of 50 feet to an inch, with the grid turned about 52 degrees on the page. Main Street crosses the middle of the part from the junction of Passaic Avenue and South Main Street, where a triangular block divides the roads, eastward towards sheet 20. North of it are Mercer Street, Cottage Place and Cottage Street with New Street and West Lane; south of it Summer Street and East Place cross Hunter, Autumn, Spring and James Streets, with Lafayette Place at the lower left. Main Street is lined with small brick and frame stores: fruit, grocery, meat, drug, dry goods and confectionery shops, barbers, a tailor, a cobbler, a bakery, a pool room, a club, a motion picture theatre and a hall and lodge room. Public buildings include the Municipal Building (stone first storey), the Second Reformed Church and parsonage, the Church of the Reformed Congregation, St. Joseph's Roman Catholic church and rectory on Spring Street, and the Church of the Lord on James Street. The blocks south of Summer Street and north of Cottage Street are residential, with two-storey frame dwellings. The Saddle River and a heavy dividing line cross the top left corner, beyond which part 2 of the sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Water pipes and hydrants are marked in the streets.
notes: Drawn at 50 feet to an inch (scale bar 'Scale of Feet'), unlike most of the volume at 100 feet.

Main Street between South Main Street and Union Street has no modern street on its line in the OpenStreetMap extract; Main Street Bypass and Memorial Drive run elsewhere. No control was taken on Main Street or north of it.
Mercer Street, Cottage Place and Cottage Street have no modern counterpart found in the extract.
Municipal Building, Second Reformed Church, St. Joseph's R.C. Church and the Church of the Lord are named on the sheet.

Lodi centre. Two parts. sheet-19-1: main map at 50 ft (Main St, Mercer, Cottage, Summer, East Pl; Hunter, Autumn, Spring, James, New, West Lane, South Main / Passaic); Main St here has no modern street on its line, control only south of Main. sheet-19-2: top-left corner beyond a heavy line along the Saddle River, at 100 ft (Westervelt Pl, Contant Av, Burns Av, Columbus School); no detectable junction, placed from one hand-picked junction plus a derived point (low confidence).

sheet-19-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 19 is a small area in its top left corner, separated by a heavy line that follows the Saddle River and then turns north. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, unlike the rest of the sheet, and shows ground in northern Lodi beyond the right edge of sheet 18: Westervelt Place runs across the top, Contant Avenue runs diagonally down to the river, and the end of Burns Avenue, continued from sheet 18, enters at the left. The large block between Westervelt Place, Contant Avenue and the river holds Columbus School, a two-storey brick building drawn from plans with tile interior walls, steam heat and electric light. Block 64, between Contant Avenue, Burns Avenue and the river, has a few two-storey frame dwellings and a pattern of lot lines; the corner of block 61 is drawn beside it. An arrow marks no exposure across the river towards the southeast.
notes: Drawn at 100 feet to an inch inside a sheet drawn at 50 feet.

No street junction is detected here; the part is placed from one hand-picked junction (Contant Avenue / Westervelt Place / Warren Street) and a derived point, so its rotation is borrowed from sheet 18.
Burns Avenue / Contant Avenue lies 67 m from Contant Avenue / Westervelt Place on the sheet but 60 m apart in the modern data, so one of the two is not on its old line.
Columbus School (block 131) is named on the sheet.

Lodi centre. Two parts. sheet-19-1: main map at 50 ft (Main St, Mercer, Cottage, Summer, East Pl; Hunter, Autumn, Spring, James, New, West Lane, South Main / Passaic); Main St here has no modern street on its line, control only south of Main. sheet-19-2: top-left corner beyond a heavy line along the Saddle River, at 100 ft (Westervelt Pl, Contant Av, Burns Av, Columbus School); no detectable junction, placed from one hand-picked junction plus a derived point (low confidence).

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 continues the centre of Lodi east of sheet 19 at 50 feet to an inch, with the grid turned about 52 degrees on the page. Main Street crosses the upper third of the sheet, lined with the town's main commercial blocks: brick stores for dry goods, hardware, drugs, meat, groceries, fruit, fish, jewellery, clothing, cigars, liquors and a five and ten cent store, barbers, a tailor, a bakery, a lunch room, offices, the post office, the First National Bank, an apartment building and McGrath's Hotel with its hall and hitching shed at Union Street. North of Main Street, Mercer Street runs along the top between Nicholson Street and Arnot Place, with dwellings, a Royal Arcanum hall, a garage and storage sheds; beyond them the southern buildings of the United Piece Dye Works (laboratory, pipe shop, creping and mercerizing building, report on sheet 18) and the Amolin Chemical Co. stock house at the top right, with a branch of the Saddle River. South of Main Street, South Place, Washington Street, Liberty Street and Union Street run down the sheet, crossed by East Place, Liberty Lane and Massey Street, which is marked not opened east of Union Street. These blocks hold frame dwellings, a few stores (bakery, wholesale liquor, grocery, confectionery) and tenements. The large block east of Union Street is almost empty, with a dash-dot line near the right edge.
notes: Drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
Main Street west of Union Street has no modern street on its line in the OpenStreetMap extract (Memorial Drive runs to the north); modern Main Street begins at Union Street.
Modern Liberty Street turns east to Union Street through drawn block 88 along a line not drawn in 1917; that junction was excluded.
Three junctions (Liberty Lane / Liberty Street, Massey Street / Union Street, Main Street / Union Street) are hand-picked; the detector paired lot lines there.
First National Bank, post office and McGrath's Hotel are named on the sheet; United Piece Dye Works report is on sheet 18.

Lodi centre east, 50 ft. One part (sheet-20). Main St, Mercer, East Pl, Liberty Lane, Massey; Nicholson, Arnot Pl, Washington, South Pl, Liberty, Union. United Piece Dye Works top, Amolin Chemical Co. Main St west of Union has no modern counterpart; three hand-picked junctions.

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 covers eastern Lodi at 100 feet to an inch, with the grid turned about 53 degrees on the page. Main Street runs diagonally across the upper part from the United Piece Dye Works at the left towards Washington School at the top right; the Saddle River winds along the top. The dye works buildings north of Main Street (dry boxes, examining, folding and laying, dyeing, doubling, finishing, machine shop and color mixing rooms, with mill-use water tanks) are drawn in detail, with a reference to the report on sheet 18; a small corner box beyond a heavy line repeats part of block 69 from sheet 18. South of Main Street, Church Street, John Street, Pond Street, Sidney Street, Victor Place and Millbank run down the sheet, crossed by Green Court, John Street, Hope Street, Boyd Street, Antonio Street, Victor Street and Massey Street; St. Joseph Street, Florence Street, Oratio Place, Chrystie Street and Shanley Place lie in the lower left corner. The New York, Susquehanna and Western Railroad crosses the sheet diagonally from the dye works towards the bottom right, with sidings to the works and the J. D. Contant coal yard. The blocks are thinly built: frame dwellings, a beer bottling works, the French Club, an Italian Club, and the F. L. Dillon Construction Co. yard full of building materials on Church Street. Large blocks 143, 158 and 267 are almost empty. Washington School is a two-storey brick building at the top right.
notes: John Street east of its bend (Pond Street to Sidney Street) is modern Money Street.
Millbank is modern Kennedy Drive; St. Joseph Street is modern Saint Joseph Boulevard; Chrystie Street is modern Christie Street.
Pond Street, Antonio Street, Florence Street and Victor Place have no match in the OpenStreetMap extract.
New York, Susquehanna and Western Railroad crosses the sheet.
Washington School, the French Club, the Italian Club and the F. L. Dillon Construction Co. are named on the sheet.

Lodi east, 100 ft. One part (sheet-21); top-left corner box beyond a heavy line repeats sheet 18 block 69 and is masked out. Main St, John, Green Court, Hope, Boyd, Massey, Antonio, Victor; Church, St Joseph, Pond, Sidney, Millbank (Kennedy Dr); Saddle River; N.Y.S.&W. railroad diagonal.

sheet-22-1.description: The main part of sheet 22 shows eastern Lodi at 100 feet to an inch, with the grid turned about 50 degrees so that Main runs across the upper part of the page from lower left to upper right and Avenues A to F run down it. Between Main and Hancock are blocks 204, 209, 210 to 212, 217 to 220 and 223, divided into long narrow lots on the Avenues; the lower blocks below Hancock (205, 208, 213, 216, 221) are laid out only as block outlines. Garibaldi Avenue, Brook and Victor cross the left side with Millbank at the left edge, in blocks 151, 152, 154 and 155. Dwellings are concentrated along Main, around Avenue A and Avenue B, and in a double row of small houses facing Avenue C in block 209, with concrete block works, a foundry and an Episcopal parsonage near Garibaldi Avenue. At the top, the Saddle River bends across the sheet beside Main, with Borig Av. and Keasler Pl. leaving it at the upper left, and the Rochelle Park Velvet Co. building stands north of Main with its admittance noted as refused. The lower right is cut off by a heavy line and forms a separate inset (part 2). A compass rose is printed near the middle of the lower margin, and the scale bar is at the bottom.
notes: Millbank is modern Kennedy Drive; Garibaldi Avenue is modern Garibaldi Avenue; Borig Avenue is modern Borig Place and Keasler Place is modern Keasler Avenue (not placed).
Main, Grant, Hancock, Brook and Victor are modern Main Street, Grant Street, Hancock Street, Brook Street and Victor Street.
Lettering at the right edge refers to The Gregg Co., 120 feet away, see Sheet 53.

Lodi east (Avenues A to F), 100 ft. Two parts. sheet-22-1: main map (Main, Grant, Hancock, Brook, Victor, Millbank (Kennedy Dr), Garibaldi Av, Borig Av, Keasler Pl, Avenues A-F; Saddle River, Rochelle Park Velvet Co). sheet-22-2: lower-right inset beyond a heavy line, Main St east of Avenue F with the Saddle River and a former flour mill; anchored on Avenue F / Main Street with the main part scale and rotation (low confidence).

sheet-22-2.description: This inset occupies the lower right corner of sheet 22, inside a heavy border, at 100 feet to an inch. It shows Main running diagonally from lower left to upper right alongside the Saddle River, which curves across the top of the inset with a mill pond and a dam. On the river bank a former flour mill, lettered as in good condition and vacant, stands with a small group of other buildings and a note that there is no watchman and no fire apparatus. South of Main, blocks 175 and 179 hold a few dwellings, a shed and an outbuilding, and the rest of the ground is unbuilt. Avenue F meets Main at the left edge of the inset, and a short stretch of it runs down the page with the number 22 printed below. A north arrow points up the page to the right. The inset shows ground east of the main part of the sheet; it is placed from the single junction of Avenue F and Main Street with the atlas scale assumed.
notes: Anchored on one junction (Avenue F / Main Street); scale and rotation are assumed from the main part. Low confidence.

Lodi east (Avenues A to F), 100 ft. Two parts. sheet-22-1: main map (Main, Grant, Hancock, Brook, Victor, Millbank (Kennedy Dr), Garibaldi Av, Borig Av, Keasler Pl, Avenues A-F; Saddle River, Rochelle Park Velvet Co). sheet-22-2: lower-right inset beyond a heavy line, Main St east of Avenue F with the Saddle River and a former flour mill; anchored on Avenue F / Main Street with the main part scale and rotation (low confidence).

sheet-58-1.description: The main part of sheet 58 covers the north edge of Hasbrouck Heights at 100 feet to an inch, with the grid turned about 52 degrees on the page. Two long streets, Oak Grove Avenue across the middle and Grandview Boulevard along the foot, are crossed by Raymond, Division, Walter, Hamilton, Franklin, Jefferson and Kipp Avenues and by Washington Park, which run down the page. Blocks 23 to 29 between Oak Grove Avenue and Grandview Boulevard are built up with frame dwellings on narrow lots, with a row of small shops and a factory building on Grandview Boulevard, a steel tower with a fire alarm bell near Jefferson Avenue and a fire alarm box at Kipp Avenue. North of Oak Grove Avenue blocks 7 to 12 are subdivided into narrow lots and mostly empty, except for a few dwellings in blocks 10 to 12. The Lodi and Hasbrouck Heights borough line crosses the upper right along a lot line just south of Woodside Avenue, and the blocks above it, numbered 237 and 48 and bounded by Terrace Avenue and Sheridan, belong to Lodi and are largely empty. A heavy line cuts off the upper left corner, which is a separate inset of Lodi at the same scale (part 2). Six-inch water pipes are marked in nearly every street, and the scale bar is printed along the bottom edge.
notes: Grandview Boulevard is modern Boulevard; Raymond Avenue is modern Raymond Street; Washington Park and Washington Avenue are modern Washington Place.
The Lodi and Hasbrouck Heights borough line is printed above Woodside Avenue.
Boulevard / Raymond Street, Boulevard / Division Avenue and Franklin Avenue / Oak Grove Avenue were left out of the control (5 to 6 m residuals).

Lodi and Hasbrouck Heights, 100 ft. Two parts. sheet-58-1: main map (Woodside, Oak Grove Avs, Grandview Blvd (Boulevard); Raymond, Division, Walter, Hamilton, Franklin, Jefferson, Kipp, Washington Park/Av (Washington Pl); Terrace, Sheridan in Lodi above the borough line). Boulevard junctions at Raymond, Division and Walter and Franklin / Oak Grove sit 5 to 7 m off and are left out. sheet-58-2: top-left Lodi inset beyond a heavy line (Millbank Bleachery, Metakloth Co, Pond; Millbank, Garabaldi Av, Victor, Mill), 3 junctions, no redundancy (low confidence).

sheet-58-2.description: This inset fills the upper left corner of sheet 58 inside a heavy border. It shows the Millbank Bleachery in Lodi, at 100 feet to an inch. A large pink brick and frame mill with a storage building, coal piles, water tanks and a pumping station stands beside a pond, with the New York, Susquehanna and Western railroad crossing the corner on several tracks. The works are labelled with their fire protection: a night watchman with a magnetic clock, automatic sprinklers, a stand pipe system, a fire pump and a fire brigade. The works lie between Millbank, which runs down the page at the left, and Garabaldi Avenue. East of Garabaldi Avenue, Metakloth Co. waterproofing duck goods occupies a building in block 135, with a concrete floor and a one night watchman noted, and the remaining blocks (152, 153, 155 and 203) are nearly empty. Victor runs across the top and Mill leaves Garabaldi Avenue on the right. A compass rose and north arrow stand at the bottom of the inset. The inset repeats ground drawn in sheet 21 and sheet 22 of the same atlas, whose numbers appear at the left and top.
notes: Millbank is modern Kennedy Drive; Garabaldi Avenue is modern Garibaldi Avenue; Victor and Mill are modern Victor Street and Mill Street.
Placed from three junctions only; the fit has no redundancy.

Lodi and Hasbrouck Heights, 100 ft. Two parts. sheet-58-1: main map (Woodside, Oak Grove Avs, Grandview Blvd (Boulevard); Raymond, Division, Walter, Hamilton, Franklin, Jefferson, Kipp, Washington Park/Av (Washington Pl); Terrace, Sheridan in Lodi above the borough line). Boulevard junctions at Raymond, Division and Walter and Franklin / Oak Grove sit 5 to 7 m off and are left out. sheet-58-2: top-left Lodi inset beyond a heavy line (Millbank Bleachery, Metakloth Co, Pond; Millbank, Garabaldi Av, Victor, Mill), 3 junctions, no redundancy (low confidence).

sheet-59.description: Sheet 59 covers the western edge of Hasbrouck Heights and the adjoining part of Woodridge at 100 feet to an inch, turned so that Grandview Boulevard crosses the upper part of the page from lower left to upper right. A borough line between Woodridge and Hasbrouck Heights runs down the left side of the sheet. East of it the blocks (numbered 16 to 20, 33 to 37, 50 to 54, 80 and 87) are laid out between Lincoln, Roosevelt, Harrison, Cleveland, Columbus, Springfield and Passaic Avenues, which run down the page, and are cut by Grandview Boulevard, Summit and Terrace Avenue. Nearly all are divided into very narrow lots, and the west side of the sheet, blocks 80 and 87, is wholly unbuilt. Dwellings, mostly frame with small outbuildings, are scattered in blocks 33 to 37 and 50 to 54, with a few stores and garages. A larger building with a blue roof stands in block 37 near Passaic Avenue. Water pipes of 6 and 24 inches are marked in Grandview Boulevard, Summit and Hackensack Avenue, and fire alarm boxes stand at Summit and Cleveland Avenue. At the bottom, Terrace Avenue turns across the sheet past Euclid Square to join Hackensack Avenue, with Main Street, Lincoln Street and Hillside Drive leaving it, and block 94 holds a garage and several scattered buildings. A compass rose and a few isolated buildings occupy the Woodridge ground in the lower left, and the scale bar is printed at the bottom edge.
notes: Grandview Boulevard is modern Boulevard; Summit is modern Summit Street.
Hackensack Avenue has no street of that name in the OpenStreetMap extract (only a Hackensack Street).
The Woodridge and Hasbrouck Heights borough line is printed down the left side of the sheet.

Woodridge and Hasbrouck Heights, 100 ft. One part. Grandview Blvd (Boulevard), Summit, Terrace Av, Euclid Sq, Hackensack Av, Lincoln St, Hillside Drive; Lincoln, Roosevelt, Harrison, Cleveland, Columbus, Springfield, Passaic Avs, Main. Woodridge / Hasbrouck Heights borough line down the left side.

sheet-60.description: Sheet 60 covers the central business and residential area of Hasbrouck Heights at 100 feet to an inch, with the street grid turned about 52 degrees on the page so that Grandview Boulevard runs along the top edge and Burton Avenue and Terrace Avenue cross the sheet. Passaic Avenue (at the left edge), Henry Street, Raymond, Division, Walter, Hamilton, Franklin and Jefferson Avenues run down the sheet between Grandview Boulevard and Terrace Avenue. The blocks between Grandview Boulevard and Burton Avenue are the most built up, with frame dwellings and a row of stores along Grandview Boulevard between Hamilton and Franklin Avenues and beyond Franklin, including a telephone exchange, shoe shop, paint shop and laundry. Institutions include the Euclid Public Schools at Passaic Avenue and Burton Avenue, the Hasbrouck Heights Field Club on Grandview Boulevard at Raymond Avenue, the First M.E. Church on Division Avenue, the Municipal Building and Fire Department on Walter Avenue (with a note on its motor truck and alarm system), Franklin School on Hamilton Avenue, the Borough League Library on Division Avenue, the Baptist Church on Walter Avenue, the Peoples Tennis Court and the Wm. M. Wheeler wood shop. South of Terrace Avenue the land is largely open: a large peach orchard with a fruit packing building (block 103), Berkshire Road laid out with a bend from Division Avenue toward Berdan Avenue, a narrow-lot subdivision between Berdan and Jefferson Avenues reaching 3rd Street, and an old line of Terrace Avenue cutting across the lower left corner past a small triangular block (105). Hillside Drive and a Passaic Avenue segment marked not opened appear at the lower left edge. The compass and scale bar sit in the open orchard area.
notes: Grandview Boulevard is modern Boulevard; Raymond Avenue is modern Raymond Street.
Berdan Avenue is not in the OpenStreetMap extract under that name; its line south of Terrace Avenue is carried by modern Franklin Avenue, which meets Berkshire Road at the drawn bend.
The old Terrace Avenue diagonal at the lower left (beside block 105) differs from the modern street line; the Passaic Avenue / Terrace Avenue junction was rejected by the fit (8.7 m).
Euclid Public Schools, Franklin School, the Municipal Building and Fire Department, the First M.E. Church and the Baptist Church are drawn.

sheet-61.description: Sheet 61 shows the central part of Hasbrouck Heights at 100 feet to an inch, turned so that Grandview Boulevard runs across the top and the cross streets run down the page. Grandview Boulevard, Burton Avenue and Terrace Avenue are the three long streets crossing the sheet; between them Jefferson, Kipp, Washington, Central, Madison, Lasalle and Ottawa Avenues cut the blocks (numbered 45 to 49, 62 to 65, 81 and 88). The two upper rows of blocks are residential, mostly frame dwellings with garages on long narrow lots, with the Pioneer Club hall (bowling and pool) at Jefferson Avenue, the Corpus Christi Roman Catholic church on Kipp Avenue and the First Reformed Church at Burton Avenue and Kipp Avenue. The Episcopal church stands in the block south of Burton Avenue at Jefferson Avenue, and the Old Homestead Hotel in block 64 on Terrace Avenue. Blocks 49, 81, 65 and 88 on the right are subdivided into very narrow unbuilt lots. Below Terrace Avenue the street pattern changes: Jefferson Avenue, Ravine Avenue and Washington Place run beside a curving ravine street, with the Hasbrouck Inn Hotel, Holmsted's Sons machine shop and the Hasbrouck Heights News Letter printing office, and a compass rose and scale bar occupy the open ground in block 108. The lower right is laid out in lettered blocks A to H between Michigan, Alger, Hasbrouck and Prospect Avenues, nearly all unbuilt. Water pipes of 6, 12 and 24 inches are marked along the streets, and fire alarm boxes stand at Burton Avenue and Washington Avenue and at Grandview Boulevard and Ottawa Avenue.
notes: Grandview Boulevard is modern Boulevard; Washington Avenue and Washington Place are modern Washington Place.
Hasbrouck Avenue and Prospect match modern Hasbrouck Avenue and Prospect Street by position here (not swapped as on the 1914 sheets).

Hasbrouck Heights, 100 ft. One part. Grandview Blvd, Burton, Terrace Avs; Jefferson, Kipp, Washington Av / Pl, Central, Madison, Lasalle, Ottawa, Michigan, Alger, Ravine Avs, 3rd St. The curved Hasbrouck Av and the Prospect east of Madison are both modern Hasbrouck Avenue; the lower Prospect is modern Prospect Street (matched by position).

sheet-62-1.description: The main part of sheet 62 covers the north end of Hasbrouck Heights at 100 feet to an inch, with the grid turned about 52 degrees on the page. Grandview Boulevard crosses the top and Burton Avenue and Terrace Avenue cross the middle, and Ottawa, Bell, Lawrence, Williams and Stanley Avenues run down the page between them, with Collins Avenue cutting the upper blocks. The blocks (numbered 75 to 93, 122 to 127, 151 to 156 and 160, 161) are mostly laid out in long, narrow lots, and the upper rows above Burton Avenue are nearly empty. Dwellings stand in blocks 84, 85, 91 and 92 around Lawrence Avenue and Burton Avenue, a fire alarm box stands at that corner, and the Lincoln Public School occupies block 89 beside Ottawa Avenue. A fire alarm bell on a steel tower stands in block 152. Below Terrace Avenue the pattern changes: Prospect Avenue, Hasbrouck Avenue, Hillside Avenue and Crescent Avenue enclose blocks 122 to 127 and 160, 161, with the Hasbrouck Heights Garage (concrete, 25 cars) in block 122 and a large unsubdivided area, with scattered houses, between Hillside Avenue and Williams Avenue. A compass rose and north arrow fill block 82 and 83. Two insets on the right, cut off by heavy lines, are separate parts (parts 2 and 3). The scale bar is printed at the bottom right.
notes: Grandview Boulevard is modern Boulevard.

On this sheet the street printed Prospect Avenue at the left (between blocks 122 and 123) lies on modern Prospect Street, while the street printed Prospect Avenue at the right (south of block 161) and Hasbrouck Avenue at the left lie on modern Hasbrouck Avenue; the street printed Crescent Avenue continues modern Prospect Street east of Williams Avenue.

Hasbrouck Avenue / Ottawa Avenue and Ottawa Avenue / Prospect Street were left out here: Ottawa Avenue below Terrace Avenue is cut by the left edge of the sheet. Sheet 61 measures both junctions within 4 m of their modern position.

sheet-62-2.description: This inset occupies the upper right corner of sheet 62, inside a heavy border, at 100 feet to an inch. It shows a short stretch of Oak Grove Avenue where the Lodi and Hasbrouck Heights borough line runs along the street, with Lodi above and Hasbrouck Heights below. Lawrence Avenue crosses Oak Grove at the left, and the street on the right edge, lettered Union at the top and Williams Avenue lower down, carries the borough line again. Above Oak Grove the Lodi blocks (numbered 119 and 120) are small, with a few dwellings, and a note records a 37 foot strip to be reserved. Below it, in Hasbrouck Heights, blocks 75 and 76 are divided into narrow lots with a handful of dwellings, and the larger part of both is empty. Six inch water pipes run in Oak Grove Avenue and Lawrence Avenue. A north arrow points up the page to the right, and the lower edge carries the dash-dot match line lettered A and B of the neighbouring parts. The inset is placed from one junction (Oak Grove Avenue and Union Street) with the atlas scale assumed.
notes: Union and Williams Avenue are modern Union Street on this stretch; Oak Grove is modern Oak Grove Avenue.
Only one junction (Oak Grove Avenue / Union Street) was measured; Lawrence Avenue / Oak Grove Avenue is about 3 percent closer on the sheet than on the modern map.

sheet-62-3.description: This inset fills the lower right corner of sheet 62 inside a heavy border, at 100 feet to an inch. It shows a strip of Hasbrouck Heights between Washington Park and Central Avenue, with Oak Grove Avenue crossing it. The upper block, numbered 13, is divided into very narrow lots and has a row of dwellings along Washington Park, with a church or public building and a small pink building, and block 14 to its right is empty. Below Oak Grove Avenue the blocks (numbered 30 and 31) are lined with frame dwellings facing Washington Avenue on the left and Central Avenue on the right, with a few garages and a pink-roofed building at the bottom, and the interior of block 30 is open. Six inch water pipes are marked in the streets and a fire alarm box stands at Oak Grove Avenue. The sheet number 61 appears at the lower edge, marking the continuation onto sheet 61, and 58 at the left marks the neighbouring sheet. A north arrow in block 30 points up the page to the right. The inset is placed from the two junctions of Oak Grove Avenue with Washington Park and Central Avenue.
notes: Washington Park and Washington Avenue are modern Washington Place.
Placed from two junctions only (helmert); scale 4.03 px/ft agrees with the atlas.
